prompt: In many countries, services that were once run by the state, such as prisons, railways and rubbish collection, are now operated by private companies under government contracts. Do you think this is a positive or a negative development?
essay:
Over recent decades, many governments have handed the day-to-day running of prisons, railways and waste collection to private firms while continuing to pay for them. Although this has improved some services, I regard the overall trend as negative, because the conditions that make private provision work are often absent.

The case for outsourcing rests on competition. A government department that performs poorly rarely faces any real consequence, whereas a contractor that misses its targets can, in principle, lose the contract to a rival. This pressure has produced genuine improvements in services where performance is easy to observe. Refuse collection is the clearest example, either the bins are emptied on the agreed day or they are not, and a council can compare the prices and records of several bidders before choosing one.

The weakness of this model is that competition only disciplines a firm when the contract can realistically be taken away. Railways and prisons are not like bin rounds. Few companies have the capital to run a rail network, so there are rarely more than a handful of bidders, and a government that dismisses a failing operator must be ready to run the trains itself the next morning. Contractors are well aware of this, which considerably weakens the state's bargaining position. In prisons the problem is compounded by the fact that the outcomes which matter most, such as whether inmates are rehabilitated, are slow to appear and hard to attribute, so a company can meet its targets on paper while cutting staff in ways that make the prison more dangerous.

For these reasons, I believe the development is negative overall. Outsourcing should be limited to services where the market is genuinely competitive and quality can be measured easily, while complex and essential services should return to direct public control.
title: Private companies running public services
